notes:
Implements only BendWire-v0 (gym_agx.envs:BendWireEnv, the first card entry symbol); BendWireObstacle-v0, PushRope-v0, PegInHole-v0, RubberBand-v0, CableClosing-v0 and the unexported InsertORing-v0 are not covered. The fake is a pure Python analytic surrogate: AGX Dynamics and its licence were not installed, the upstream package was never imported or run, and the sim backend (upstream AGX) was not exercised. The fake's start jitter, curvature length 8 and goal array are test data, not facts; the real curvature array has one value per adjacent cable-segment pair (about 100 values for the 0.1 m cable at 1000 segments per metre, gym_agx/utils/utils.py:243-248 and gym_agx/sims/bend_wire.py:36-39), and AGX sets the exact count when it initializes the cable in the binary gym_agx/envs/assets/bend_wire.agx scene, which the package does not parse. The fidelity contract is F1 for the deployed AGX model, but its determinism note and gaps disclose that BendWireEnv.reset() takes no seed and the class defines no seed method of its own (gym_agx/envs/agx_goal_env.py:133-134 and :180), so cap.world.seed.v1 can only be shown to seed the package fake. Warnings left as family-bridge limitations, as in the exemplar: G6.NO_NATIVE_CALL for cap.world.seed.v1 (the seed is queued for the next reset and makes no native call) and four G8.NO_UNIT messages (ticks, action.values[*], and the reset and seed inputs). No G4.REF_VALUE or G4.REF_BINARY warnings. No extension capability ids were used, so no catalogue_requests are needed. No hardware backend was used or claimed; the device is simulated R0 under the runtime's software e-stop latch.
